translation_notes: context_shim.py restores `from ..rdflib import DefinedNamespace, Namespace, URIRef` and `from ..typing import Final`, relative imports that need a real parent package; kif_lib/rdflib.py and kif_lib/typing.py are themselves pure re-exports (no wrapping), so the shim mirrors them. This is the same pattern already used for the sibling region kif_lib/namespace/semsci.py in this stratum.

NOT-EXPRESSIBLE, the exact case the batch brief warns about: `_NS = Namespace('http://purl.uniprot.org/core/')` is a class attribute of `class UNIPROT(DefinedNamespace)`. rdflib's DefinedNamespace.__getattr__/__getitem__ reads `cls._NS` on EVERY attribute access (rdflib/namespace/__init__.py:290-301) -- not just at definition time. The `Taxon: URIRef`, `rank: URIRef`, etc. lines are bare annotations holding no value; the URIRef only exists lazily, produced by that `_NS` lookup. `@prefix uniprot: <...> .` transpiles to a transpile-time binding-table entry, not a class attribute -- it leaves no `_NS` for rdflib to find.

unlike the semsci sibling, nothing INSIDE this 73-line region itself reads a UNIPROT attribute (there is no local CHEMINF/SIO-style class deriving from it here), so the substitution alone does not raise merely by running the module -- the failure is invisible unless something calls e.g. UNIPROT.Taxon, exactly what a DefinedNamespace subclass exists to be imported and used for elsewhere in kif_lib. Added an identical harness-only probe to both original.py and translated.ldpy, `PROBE = str(UNIPROT.Taxon)`, documented in place, to make that downstream failure observable to `rdfeval check` without inventing any other logic.

`rdfeval check` on this pair: original.py runs to completion (PROBE = 'http://purl.uniprot.org/core/Taxon'); translated.ldpy raises at the probe line, `AttributeError: DefinedNamespace like object has no attribute '_NS'`. `class UNIPROT(DefinedNamespace): @prefix uniprot: <...> .` plus any later `UNIPROT.Something` is the minimal extract that shows the limit.

the separate `class UniProt(Namespace)` a few lines below has the SAME limit from a different angle, left untouched (not substituted) because one demonstration per file is enough: `TAXONOMY: Final[Namespace] = Namespace('http://purl.uniprot.org/taxonomy/')` is a Namespace OBJECT stored as a class attribute and then as a dict VALUE (`namespaces = {str(TAXONOMY): TAXONOMY}`), consumed elsewhere as `UniProt.namespaces[iri]`. `@prefix` has no runtime object at all, so there is nothing to put in that dict -- confirming this batch's finding that a Namespace escaping into a container or an attribute, not just a return value, is equally out of reach.
translation_status stays draft and cannot go final: there is no notation that covers a DefinedNamespace-style exported registry without changing kif_lib's own contract with its callers.
